metadata.title: Alternative routes in use after the 26 August 2026 Bhote Koshi / Trishuli flood

confidence.mapped: geometry taken from OpenStreetMap way geometry or a surveyed point
confidence.approximate: coarse polyline or point through the waypoints that could be geolocated

metadata.caveat: Route names come from NDRRMA situation reports and press. Many intermediate waypoints are not in OpenStreetMap or Nominatim, so approximate geometries show the corridor, not the alignment. Do not use for navigation.

properties.name: Trishuli right-bank detour (Galchhi - Gauribesi - Trishuli Bazaar)
properties.route: Galchhi - Trishuli Bridge - Kalleritar - Koshikhola - Pimaltar - Darshantar - Chhatre Khola - Gauribesi - Trishuli Bazaar
properties.users: general traffic, relief convoys from Dhading and the Prithvi Highway
properties.notes: Listed as operational in NDRRMA SitRep #15. Crosses the Trishuli on the intact Bhimdhunga-Lamidanda road bridge at Galchhi, then runs up the right (west) bank, avoiding all the destroyed left-bank bridges. Narrow single lane, slow, difficult for two-way traffic. Geometry traced 400 m west of the OSM Trishuli centreline; Kalleritar, Koshikhola, Pimaltar, Darshantar and Chhatre Khola could not be geolocated.

properties.name: Ratmate bypass track (Galchhi - Bidur)
properties.route: new hill-cut track above the washed-out Pasang Lhamu Highway at Ratmate, rejoining via Dui Pipal
properties.users: Department of Roads works traffic, then general traffic
properties.notes: OSM way 1559050050, highway=primary, ref=NH42, note="Under construction to bypass damaged section", tagged damaged:event=2026NepalFlood. Matches the Kathmandu Post report of 13 Sep: new track above the flood-washed section at Ratmate, about 8 km from Galchhi, adding roughly 3 km to the journey and rejoining at Dui Pipal village, expected complete around 14 Sep (DoR deputy director Shubha Raj Neupane).

properties.name: Devighat Acrow bridge over the Tadi Khola
properties.route: Pasang Lhamu Highway at Devighat, Bidur
properties.users: all traffic on the Galchhi-Devighat-Trishuli road
properties.notes: 60 m Acrow bridge, 5.5 m wide, 50-tonne capacity, built in five days by a 55-member Nepal Army Bridging Unit team at the site of the destroyed 55 m Tadi Khola bridge. Opened to pedestrians 10 Sep, vehicles from 11 Sep. NDRRMA SitRep #15 confirms Galchhi-Devighat is clear and operational, with Kolphu Khola bridge on one-lane traffic.
properties.source: Meroauto - Rs 32.5m allocated for road repairs as Bailey bridges planned at three sites

properties.name: Devighat bridge bypass (Pipaltar - Kolputar)
properties.route: Pipaltar - Pasang Lhamu Highway - Dhamle - Niranjana - Bagkhor - Harre - Deurali - Kolputar
properties.users: local traffic bypassing the destroyed Tadi Khola bridge
properties.notes: Listed as operational in NDRRMA SitRep #15 as the alternative to the damaged Devighat bridge, with maintenance continuing. Only Pipaltar and Devighat could be geolocated; Dhamle, Niranjana, Bagkhor, Harre, Deurali and Kolputar are not in OSM or Nominatim, so the line is a coarse connector, not a surveyed alignment.

properties.name: Devighat rope crossing (tuin)
properties.route: across the Trishuli at Devighat
properties.users: residents cut off by the destroyed Devighat suspension bridge
properties.notes: NDRRMA SitRep #15: "Rope crossings have been completed at Devighat, Indreni Chaur and Syafrubesi." Placed at the destroyed Devighat suspension bridge recorded in the DoR inventory; the rope may be strung a short distance away.

properties.name: Bidur - Betrawati road (Pasang Lhamu Highway, partly restored)
properties.route: Bidur - Trishuli Bazaar - Tupche - Dhunge Bazar - Betrawati
properties.users: Department of Roads plant, relief vehicles, light 4WD
properties.notes: NDRRMA SitRep #15: of the 10 km section, 9.2 km is clear; the remaining 0.8 km was completely washed away; restoration includes cutting 0.5 km of hard rock, with graveling ongoing and landslides plus waterlogged ground still affecting work on the new and existing tracks. Kathmandu Post 13 Sep put it at 9.5 km opened with 500 m remaining. Geometry traced along the OSM Trishuli centreline, offset east; the new hill-cut track is not yet in OSM.

properties.name: Gerkhu - Bhainse feeder around the Betrawati gap
properties.route: Bidur - Gerkhu - Bhainse - Betrawati; final 300 m either a riverbed track or the Bar Bhanjyang local road
properties.users: works traffic and local people crossing the 500-800 m washed-out gap
properties.notes: Kathmandu Post 13 Sep: a 1.5 km feeder route through Gerku/Bhainse covers the remaining 500 m gap, with two options for the final 300 m, a riverbed track or the Bar Bhanjyang local road. The feeder itself is about 1.5 km; this line spans the wider Gerkhu-Bhainse-Betrawati detour because the feeder endpoints are not published. Gerkhu and Bhainse coordinates are from OSM place nodes; the track itself is not in OSM.
properties.source: Kathmandu Post - Flood damage leaves Rasuwagadhi road facing long repairs

properties.name: Betrawati temporary footbridge (~30 m)
properties.route: across the Phalankhu/Trishuli at Betrawati, Bidur-10
properties.users: residents, porters carrying relief across the gap
properties.notes: NDRRMA SitRep #14 (15 Sep): "A temporary footbridge approximately 30 metres long has been rebuilt at Betrawati, Bidur-10." Still listed in the 16 Sep report. Placed at the site of the destroyed Betrawati old and new bridges (70 m each) in the DoR inventory. This is currently the only fixed crossing at Betrawati.

properties.name: Betrawati Bailey bridge (foundation excavation)
properties.route: Pasang Lhamu Highway crossing at Betrawati
properties.users: not yet open
properties.notes: NDRRMA SitRep #15: "Foundation excavation is underway for a Bailey bridge at Betrawati." DoR had specified roughly a 48 m span. The Nepal Army bridging team moved here after finishing Devighat. Not open as of 16 Sep.

properties.name: Falakhu Khola 70 m Bailey bridge (Indian-supplied, planned)
properties.route: Rasuwa-Nuwakot boundary just north of Betrawati
properties.users: not yet open
properties.notes: Kathmandu Post 13 Sep: a 70 m Bailey bridge is planned at Falakhu Khola on the Rasuwa-Nuwakot border; the Indian-supplied bridge was en route from Hetauda, with DoR deputy director Shubha Raj Neupane saying "we expect to install it within ten days". India handed over the first components on 12 Sep. Once in, it would give a direct road connection to Dhunche. Location approximated at the confluence north of Betrawati; the exact site is not published.
properties.source: Kathmandu Post - Flood damage leaves Rasuwagadhi road facing long repairs

properties.name: Kalikasthan - Dhunche (Pasang Lhamu Highway, 4WD only)
properties.route: Bogatitar - Kalikasthan - Ramche - Dhunche
properties.users: relief convoys, district administration, local traffic
properties.notes: OSM ways 27033235, 344160418, 344160419, 934778608, 934778609 (highway=primary, ref=NH18/NH42) carry the note: "Only small vehicles (4 x 4 jeeps) are allowed. Caution due to risk of landslides. Not advised to travel the route at night. Relief vehicles should register with the police in Kalikasthan before driving to Dhunche." Kathmandu Post 8 Sep records the Bogatitar-Kalikasthan-Dhunche section reopened to light four-wheel drive only.

properties.name: Kathmandu - Tokha - Saramthali - Bogatitar route to Rasuwa
properties.route: Kathmandu - Tokha - Chhahare - Gadkhar Bridge - Aapre - Narja - Lachyang - Saramthali - Patikharka - Bogatitar - Kalikasthan - Dhunche
properties.users: relief convoys and government traffic; the main lifeline to Rasuwa
properties.notes: Announced by the Ministry of Physical Infrastructure and Transport and reported reopened on 28 Aug 2026, two days after the flood. Restricted to light four-wheeled vehicles; heavy trucks excluded. Only Tokha, Chhahare, Narjamandap and Lachyang could be geolocated in OSM; Gadkhar Bridge, Aapre, Saramthali, Patikharka and Bogatitar could not, so this is a coarse ridge-route trace, not a surveyed alignment.
properties.source: OnlineKhabar - Rasuwa reconnected to road network after devastating floods

properties.name: Dhikure - Jibjibe - Bogatitar route (Nuwakot side)
properties.route: Dhikure - Phedi Besi Chowk - Hiramunitar - Chogte - Bore Bhanjyang - Sano Khola - Dhanswara - Bhorle - Jibjibe - Bogatitar
properties.users: traffic from Nuwakot to Rasuwa while the Trishuli-Betrawati highway is out
properties.notes: NDRRMA SitRep #15 lists this as operational, "providing alternative access while the Trishuli-Betrawati highway section remains damaged", with maintenance continuing. SitRep #14 phrased it as "the alternative route to Rasuwa through Dhikure-Jibjibe-Bogatitar is now operational". Dhikure and Jibjibe are from Nominatim; the intermediate ridge points could not be geolocated.

properties.name: Betrawati - Kalikasthan (Pasang Lhamu Highway) - the link the detours replace
properties.route: Betrawati - Khalte - Ramche - Kalikasthan
properties.users: closed to through traffic
properties.notes: Context feature, not an alternative. The normal highway link. DoR records the Betrawati old and new bridges (70 m each) and the Naya Pul Trishuli at Khalte (50 m) as washed out; Copernicus EMSR927 grades stretches of the Pasang Lhamu Highway here Destroyed. Traffic uses DH-2 or DH-3 instead.
properties.source: Department of Roads bridge-damage inventory (HDX / HOT flood_npl bridge_damage)

properties.name: Dhunche onward to Syabrubesi and Rasuwagadhi
properties.route: Dhunche - Thulo Bharkhu - Syabrubesi - Timure - Rasuwagadhi
properties.mode: none - helicopter, drone and rope crossings only
properties.users: no vehicle traffic; supplies move by air
properties.notes: Beyond Dhunche "the road is gone" (Urken Chiring Lama, Kathmandu Post 8 Sep). DoR records the Syafrubesi bridge, the Bhotekoshi and Chilime bridges and the Haku Bailey bridges all washed out. Target is a temporary track to Rasuwagadhi by Dashain via multiple Bailey bridges (Kathmandu Post 13 Sep).
properties.source: Kathmandu Post - Dhunche has relief supplies; getting aid to villages is the problem

properties.name: Helicopter lifeline from Dhunche to cut-off Rasuwa villages
properties.route: Dhunche staging area to Mailung, Haku, Syabrubesi and upper Gosaikunda wards
properties.users: NDRRMA, Nepal Army, ward chairpersons moving relief
properties.notes: Relief is staged at Dhunche and flown onward. NDRRMA SitRep #15 reports 1,694 helicopter sorties in total. The bottleneck is slots, not stock: ward chairman Mansing Tamang had waited three days in Dhunche to fly 250 sacks of rice to Mailung (Kathmandu Post, 8 Sep). The Nepal Army also flies Chinese-supplied drones, useful only for small consignments (Sang Lama). Straight line, indicative of the air link only.
properties.source: Kathmandu Post - Dhunche has relief supplies; getting aid to villages is the problem

properties.name: Uttargaya emergency helipad (Mailung area)
properties.route: Uttargaya rural municipality, Rasuwa
properties.users: relief flights to Mailung and Uttargaya
properties.notes: OSM node 3498339453, tagged emergency_helipad=potential, status Standing, in the HDX/HOT flood_npl helipad layer. Mailung is road-cut: the Trishuli-Mailung-Syabrubesi road was washed away and relief reaches it by air.

properties.name: Syafrubesi rope crossing (tuin)
properties.route: across the Bhotekoshi at Syabrubesi
properties.users: residents of Gosaikunda wards cut off by the destroyed Syafrubesi bridge
properties.notes: NDRRMA SitRep #15 lists rope crossings completed at Devighat, Indreni Chaur and Syafrubesi. Placed at the destroyed Syafrubesi bridge in the DoR inventory. The Kathmandu Post of 8 Sep described a planned crossing of the Bhotekoshi between Syabrubesi and Chilime.

properties.name: Hakubesi rope crossing (ordered, not yet complete)
properties.route: across the Trishuli at Haku Besi, Gosaikunda
properties.users: Haku residents
properties.notes: NDRRMA SitRep #15: "Instructions have been issued to expedite two additional crossings at Hakubesi and Pahirebesi." Coordinates from the OSM Haku Besi place node; the crossing point itself is not published.

properties.name: Pahirebesi - Shantibazar rope crossing (ordered, not yet complete)
properties.route: across the Trishuli between Pahirebesi (Uttargaya-4) and Shantibazar (Kispang-5, Nuwakot)
properties.users: Uttargaya and Kispang residents, including Simle and Shanti Bazaar which lost all road access
properties.notes: Kathmandu Post 8 Sep lists a planned Trishuli crossing between Pahirebesi and Shantibazar; NDRRMA SitRep #15 orders it expedited. Neither settlement is in OSM or Nominatim; the point is inferred from the Uttargaya-Kispang boundary on the Trishuli near the intact Sukaure Khola bridge, so it may be off by a few kilometres.
properties.source: Kathmandu Post - Dhunche has relief supplies; getting aid to villages is the problem
